# Incident Report — MTA 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.11.26.183** | Consistent source IP across all suspicious traffic |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** | ARP: `10.11.26.183 -> d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b` (only MAC ever bound to this IP in the capture) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (NetBIOS name **NEMOTODES**, domain **NEMOTODES**) | NBNS: `DESKTOP-B8TQK49<00>`/`<20>` and `NEMOTODES<00>`/`<1e>` both sourced from 10.11.26.183; DNS queries for `DESKTOP-B8TQK49` / `DESKTOP-B8TQK49.local` |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** (Oliver Q. Boomwald) | Kerberos `CNameString=oboomwald` in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.11.26.183 and the DC; confirmed by LDAP search result `CN=Oliver Q.. Boomwald,CN=Users,DC=nemotodes,DC=health` |
| Domain controller | 10.11.26.3 (NEMOTODE-DC / DC=nemotodes,DC=health; SRV records also resolve under `nemotoads.health`) | NBNS, LDAP, Kerberos traffic |
| Gateway | 10.11.26.1 (MAC 00:17:e0:b8:29:5e) | ARP |

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT (NetSupport Manager abused as a remote-access trojan).**

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The Suricata/ET alert export contains direct hits: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`, and `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`, all tied to the 10.11.26.183 ↔ 194.180.191.64 conversation.

This is corroborated behaviorally: following TCP stream 77 (10.11.26.183:53362 ↔ 194.180.191.64:443) shows plaintext HTTP (not actual TLS, despite the destination port) with:
```
POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm HTTP/1.1
User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3
...
CMD=POLL
INFO=1
ACK=1
```
and server responses `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.8 (Windows NT)` returning `CMD=ENCD` / encrypted `DATA=` payloads. This exact `CMD=POLL`/`CMD=ENCD` exchange is the NetSupport Manager client-gateway protocol, confirming an active NetSupport RAT implant beaconing to attacker infrastructure. The client also performed a legitimate NetSupport geolocation lookup (`GET /location/loca.asp` to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com`, 104.26.1.231) immediately before check-in started, which is stock NetSupport client startup behavior.

**Delivery chain (behavioral, not signature-confirmed for the redirect hops):** DNS/TLS-SNI timing shows the victim visiting `classicgrand.com` (213.246.109.5) then `confirmsubscription.com` (52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207) then `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139) within a 34-second window at 04:50:11–04:50:45 UTC, immediately followed by the first NetSupport RAT check-in at 04:50:45 UTC. `modandcrackedapk.com` is flagged by name via `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in TLS SNI` — consistent with a cracked-software/mod-APK lure site used to trojanize a NetSupport installer. The actual installer transfer itself is TLS-encrypted to 193.42.38.139 and cannot be recovered from the capture without decryption keys, so this hop is grounded as circumstantial/behavioral, not confirmed by content inspection.

Separately, the ETPRO EFSR (`EfsRpcOpenFileRaw`) and GPL NETBIOS SMB alerts at 04:49:55–04:50:10 UTC are all victim→DC (10.11.26.3) traffic occurring before the malicious DNS activity begins, consistent with routine domain-joined workstation authentication/logon (Group Policy, NTLM auth over legacy SMBv1) rather than lateral movement or exploitation. No coerced authentication back from the DC to an external host was observed. This is noted as benign context, not an IOC.
